note: See-also links between vocabularies and between collections. Hand-written, never derived. `by: proposed` means written by the tool and not yet ruled on: the library shows it as PROPOSED and uses it for nothing else. To rule, change `by` to a name and add a date, or delete the row.

relations.consequence-of: the first is the mark, the second is the process that causes it
relations.narrower: the first is a constrained case of the second
relations.part-of: the first is one run inside the second
relations.same-subject: different plates on one physical subject
relations.also-filed-as: two records that look like one work filed twice
relations.source-of: the first is where the second came from

links.basis: Same id. Both are a mean-preserving tooth that ink and paper share. Filed as a technique read in one vocabulary and an atom in the other.
The plate offset is what a second drum missing register looks like.
Both carry tone as dot radius on a regular lattice. The atom fixes pitch and angle.
A dot lattice with radius read from a tone field; the atom is the shared engine for the same job.
Both decide per pixel which of two levels prints. One threshold is random, the other ordered.
Beat fringes from two periodic screens: a product of ring gratings, and a ruling over its rotated copy.
Both are how an ink edge misbehaves: a blur-and-threshold swell, and a turbulence displacement.
Both are a one-dimensional ramp indexed by a scalar. The atom also fixes the interpolation space.
A 256-entry color table indexed by one coordinate.
The keyline run, separated from the color fills and kept in register.
Crossed-polar birefringence. One plate draws the conditions, the other computes the colors.
Same name. A post defocus on one side, a proposed technique with a bokeh atom on the other.
Both are a line-fidelity test on two subjects, one botanical and one mechanical.
The keyline and riso studies the encyclopedia technique was rebuilt from.
